title: CUDASTF: Bridging the Gap Between CUDA and Task Parallelism
problem: Current CUDA programming models lack efficient support for expressing computation as asynchronous tasks with data-driven dependencies at scale. Existing approaches require manual coordination of multi-GPU execution and cannot automatically optimize kernel placement across devices.
motivation: Task-based parallelism provides a simpler, more composable programming model for GPU applications, and optimizing this model can deliver significant performance gains for multi-GPU systems.
method: CUDASTF is a C++ library where you describe your computation as a task graph—specifying which tasks depend on which other tasks' data—and it automatically distributes those tasks across multiple GPUs with fine-grained placement control. It uses events—signals that fire when data is ready—to coordinate task execution. The library can transparently switch between CUDA Streams (traditional sequential GPU work) and CUDA Graphs (pre-optimized sequences of operations), preferring Graphs for small tasks where they're more efficient.
key_novelty: It bridges your task-level code with GPU optimizations using events (signals that fire when data is ready), enabling automatic and efficient execution across multiple GPUs without manual work distribution.
contributions: CUDASTF library implementing Sequential Task Flow model over CUDA with automatic multi-GPU support
Event-based architecture for efficient asynchronous task scheduling and kernel execution
Transparent selection between CUDA Graphs and streams with up to 30% single-GPU performance improvement
Demonstration of first multi-device implementation of CKKS fully homomorphic encryption
